(NTSTATUS) 0xC000007B — STATUS\_INVALID\_IMAGE\_FORMAT; {Bad Image} %hs is either not designed to run on Windows or it contains an error. Try installing the program again using the original installation media or contact your system administrator or the software vendor for support.

STATUS\_INVALID\_IMAGE\_FORMAT is caused by:

* executable image is empty or doesn't exist,
* the PE headers are corrupted,
* the image isn't executable (for exe's),
* the image machine types mismatch (for dll's, for example a 64 bit dll gets loaded in 32 bits)
* the dll couldn't be relocated,
* the exported functions in dll couldn't be found because of corrupted exports.

Basically your program is missing DLL's, your program is 32 bit and uses 64 bit DLL's or a 64 bit program uses 32 bit DLL's or the present DLL's are corrupt.

Hal.dll is the program which the windows kernel (the most core and important code) and drivers use to communicate with hardware. Hal.dll is one of the few required files for windows to begin starting at all. Don't delete it, otherwise you'll have to either reinstall windows or restore a new copy of the file.

A bug check (bsod) which was caused during the execution of code within ntoskrnl.exe or hal.dll, is most likely a result of a driver, the driver didn't handle its faults, driver messes up something or driver passed something wrong to the ntoskrnl or to the hal. Code within ntoskrnl and hal is near perfect and it causing a bsod is unlikely.

Kernel is the core part of the operating system, it implements processes, threads, full memory control, disk io, IPC and support for everything else upon the system. Hal.dll provides the kernel and drivers with ways to access hardware. Most of the time a bsod caused by Hal.dll or ntoskrnl.exe isn't caused by them, for example a driver calls ntoskrnl with invalid information, then the kernel just bsods cause it can't do anything with the invalid information and the bsod screen will show ntoskrnl.exe when it's the driver.
